1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Nf3 e4 4.Ng5.strategy: Answers the pawn thrust by moving the attacked knight with a new attack: e4 is now hit twice, by the knights on c3 and g5, and defended only by the knight on f6. Black must defend the pawn, counter or offer a gambit.

1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Nf3 e4 4.Ng5 c6.strategy: Prepares to support the pawn on e4 with a pawn on d5 instead of defending it directly. Black lets White win the pawn in return for development and central play, a gambit that is offbeat and gives White the choice.
1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Nf3 e4 4.Ng5 c6.name: English Opening: King's English Variation, Adhiban Gambit

1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Nf3 e4 4.Ng5 b5.strategy: Offers the b-pawn to deflect the c4 pawn and open lines on the queenside, but the pawn on e4 stays attacked twice and White can take material with cxb5 or Nxb5. Black has too little to show for the pawns.
1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Nf3 e4 4.Ng5 b5.name: English Opening: King's English Variation, Bellon Gambit

1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Nf3 e4 4.Ng5 Ng4.strategy: Leaves the pawn on e4 without any defender: it is attacked by the knights on c3 and g5, so White simply takes it. The knight on g4 eyes f2 and h2, but the king guards f2 and White can chase it away with h3.
1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.Nf3 e4 4.Ng5 Ng4.name: English Opening: King's English, Erbenheimer Gambit
